screen.description:
Which display they come on: "focused" (the one you are on), or a connector's name ("DP-1"); while that one is not there, the focused one.

Takes a text. Default: "focused".

low.description: Takes a whole number, -1 and up. Default: 4000.

normal.description: Takes a whole number, -1 and up. Default: 8000.

critical.description: Takes a whole number, -1 and up. Default: -1.

clampMin.description: Takes a whole number, 0 and up. Default: 3000.

clampMax.description: Takes a whole number, 0 and up. Default: 60000.

timeouts.description:
How long a toast stays, per urgency. A sender's own timeout is honoured
but clamped to [clampMin, clampMax]; its "never" (0) is honoured for
normal and critical only. Shell sources (timers, battery, ...) choose
their own, or take a `sources` rule below.

max.description:
toasts at once; older ones file into the manager ("+N more")

Takes a whole number, 1 and up. Default: 5.

floodCount.description:
more than this many from one app inside floodWindowMs (0: no limit)...

Takes a whole number, 0 and up. Default: 3.

floodWindowMs.description:
...and the rest file silently ("<app> . +N more")

Takes a whole number, 0 and up. Default: 10000.

hoverResumeMinMs.description:
after a hover (or being away) a toast has at least this left

Takes a whole number, 0 and up. Default: 2000.

swipe.description: What swiping a toast away does, to each side: "file" (it goes into the manager) | "delete".

openGroup.description:
The group that is open when the manager opens: "latest" (of the newest notification) | "first" | "none" | "critical" | "system" |
"normal" | "low".

Takes "latest", "first", "none", "critical", "system", "normal" or "low". Default: "latest".

swipe.description: What swiping a card does, to each side: "pin" | "delete".

clickFocus.description:
A click on a card that has no action of its own brings its app's window to the front (its workspace with it). true | false.

Takes true or false. Default: true.

bell.description: The bell rings (its glyph moves) for a new notification: "always" | "notDnd" (not while do-not-disturb is on) | "never".

count.description: Takes a whole number, -1 and up. Default: 200.

days.description: Takes a number, -1 and up. Default: 7.

retention.description:
History in the manager: the newest `count`, none older than `days`
since its last update. Pinned notifications are never dropped.

undoMs.description:
How long "Undo" is offered after Clear / Clear all.

Takes a whole number, 1 and up. Default: 10000.

idleMs.description:
No input for this long = you are away: toast countdowns stop until you are back.

Takes a whole number, 1 and up. Default: 60000.

low.description: Takes a list of paths. Default: [].

normal.description: Takes a list of paths. Default: ["~/.local/share/sounds/notification.mp3","/usr/share/sounds/notification.mp3"].

critical.description: Takes a list of paths. Default: ["~/.local/share/sounds/notification-critical.mp3","~/.local/share/sounds/notification.mp3","/usr/share/sounds/notification.mp3"].

soundVolume.description:
How loud they are, 0 .. 1; -1 plays them at the level of the sound server's stream.

Takes a number -1 .. 1. Default: -1.

remember.description:
Do-not-disturb is kept across a restart of the shell. false: it starts off.

Takes true or false. Default: true.

hours.description:
Quiet hours: do-not-disturb is on between these times ("22:30-07:00", several allowed), and off again at their end. You can still
switch it by hand in between; the next start or end of an hour goes by the clock again. [] = none.

Takes a list of texts. Default: [].

summary.description:
The summary toast ("4 while you were sharing") when a hold ends. true | false.

Takes true or false. Default: true.

holdApps.description:
Window classes that hold toasts back while one of them has the focus (a game that is not fullscreen, a presentation).

Takes a list of texts. Default: [].

breakthroughSources.description:
Shell sources that still toast under Do Not Disturb (criticals always do).

Takes a list of texts. Default: ["clock","auth"].

holdFullscreen.description:
Hold toasts back while a window is fullscreen (on the display the toasts come on) / the screen is shared
or recorded; one summary toast comes when it ends. A critical still
shows during a share.

Takes true or false. Default: true.

holdScreencast.description: Takes true or false. Default: true.

apps.description:
Per-app rules, matched on the notification's desktop entry first, then
its app name (case-insensitive, ".desktop" ignored). Keys:
  "mute": true          no toast, no sound, still in the manager
  "urgency": "low" | "normal" | "critical"
  "group": "critical" | "system" | "normal" | "low"
  "timeoutMs": 5000     overrides whatever the app asked for
  "sound": "/path/to/file.oga" or "none"
  "breakDnd": true      toasts under Do Not Disturb, whatever its urgency
  "drop": true          no toast, no sound, NOTHING filed: the sender is told Dismissed at once
                        (the OSD tells the network and bluetooth news, so the two applets are dropped)
  "history": false      never written to the history file
  "focusSuppress": true file silently while the app's own window is
                        focused (the default; kitty is exempt so a
                        terminal's notifications still show)

Default: {"kitty":{"focusSuppress":false},"org.freedesktop.network-manager-applet":{"drop":true},"NetworkManager Applet":{"drop":true},"nm-applet":{"drop":true},"blueman":{"drop":true},"blueman-applet":{"drop":true}}.

finished.description: Takes true or false. Default: true.

rebootPackages.description:

Takes a list of texts. Default: ["linux","linux-lts","linux-zen","linux-hardened","linux-rt","linux-rt-lts","systemd","mesa"].

update.description:
THE SYSTEM UPDATE. A nudge once the machine has been up a while, and the update run's own
cards while the update popup is shut.

enabled.description: Takes true or false. Default: true.

timeoutMs.description: Takes a whole number, -1 and up.

levels.description:
The charge falling to one of these, while discharging, puts ONE card up; each deeper level replaces
the one before; charging takes it away. The order here does not matter. A Critical card breaks
do-not-disturb. "hibernate" puts the Hibernate button on the card; "timeoutMs" is how long the card
stays (absent: the urgency's own; -1: until you act); "title" names the level yourself. A level is a share of the pack the
charge limit leaves: with the 80 % limit on, 8 speaks at 6.

Takes a list of objects. Default: [{"pct":8,"urgency":"critical","hibernate":true,"breakDnd":false,"timeoutMs":60000},{"pct":3,"urgency":"critical","hibernate":true,"breakDnd":true,"timeoutMs":-1}].

hibernate.description:
What the Hibernate button does: "dud" says hibernate is not set up yet (the machine has no resume
device); "systemctl" runs `systemctl hibernate`, for the day it works.

Takes "dud" or "systemctl". Default: "dud".

limitReached.description:
"Charged to 80 %": the pack reached its charge limit (or 100). Off: the OSD's battery card says it.

Takes true or false. Default: false.

enabled.description: Takes true or false. Default: true.

fastDrain.description:
A runaway process: the draw stays `factor` times above the usual (and over `minW` watts) for
`minutes`. The usual is eased over `tauMin` minutes, kept across restarts, and not judged for the
first `warmupMin` minutes of learning.

battery.description: THE BATTERY. Fed by silicon's battery (the one reader the shell has).

sudden.description: Takes true or false. Default: true.

scope.description:

stocks.description:
THE STOCKS. The alerts of stocks.jsonc (a day move, a price above, a price below) are cards of a
normal urgency like any other: they stay their 8 s ("timeoutMs" here gives them another time, -1
keeps them until you answer) and wait in the manager. The sudden move is an alert kind of its own:
a stock that moves at least X % within Y minutes while its market is open (X and Y, with numbers
per symbol, are in stocks.jsonc under "sudden"), once per direction per day.

toast.description:
"auto": while the OSD shows its card, this one is filed silently (no second popup over the same
picture); if the OSD posts a notification of its own it stays out; where the OSD says nothing it toasts.
"always" toasts as well, "never" only files.

Takes "auto", "always" or "never". Default: "auto".

screenshot.description:
A SCREENSHOT taken (tools/osd/shot.sh tells the OSD, which shows its capture card with the picture). This is
the same shot as a card that WAITS in the manager: the picture, Open, Edit (swappy), Copy path.

sources.description:
The shell's own sources. The nine below are services of their own with keys of their own:
"update", "battery", "stocks", "screenshot", "usb", "calendar", "disk", "units", "thermal". Each has
  "enabled": true       false switches the source off -- its card goes
                        with it -- and true brings it back; the file is
                        read hot
The other names things are posted under: "clock", "launcher", "llm", "auth", "notifications", "aerial", "panorama",
"silicon", "wiki", "weather", "bridge", "dictation", "shell", "session", "theme", "osd", "config" (a mistake in one of these
files). They have no switch: "mute": true keeps one quiet.
Every block takes the rule keys an app's takes (mute, urgency, group, timeoutMs, sound, breakDnd, drop, history). "timeoutMs" counts
where the post gives no time of its own; most are silent until "sound" names a file (the clock's alarms ring by themselves);
"focusSuppress" is for apps alone (a source has no window).
A key with the wrong type, or a number or word outside what it allows, is
named in the shell's log and keeps the value written here.
